content.thinking:
There's no deployment on record, but request volume jumps 4.5x starting at 21:46, and CPU usage climbs alongside it while the CPU limit itself keeps flip-flopping between 3.0 and 6.0 cores every couple minutes, which looks like something is repeatedly scaling the limit up and down rather than holding steady.

Latency p50/p95/p99 spike badly whenever the limit drops to 3 and usage saturates it, then partially recovers when the limit jumps back to 6 - this oscillation against steadily climbing (then plateauing) demand is the classic autoscaling-pathology signature, with error rates staying low throughout despite the latency swings.

No deployment or config changes appear in the window, ruling out bad-deployment or config-induced causes. The rule that cpu_limit_cores taking multiple values should point to autoscaling-pathology over demand-saturation clinches it, so I'll finalize autoscaling-pathology as the primary hypothesis with high confidence, noting demand-saturation as a plausible secondary factor given the 4.5x traffic increase.

Confirming further, traffic actually plateaus at 5400 after 21:56, yet cpu_limit_cores keeps oscillating between 6 and 3 repeatedly—so capacity keeps flapping even though demand has stabilized, which rules out simple demand outgrowing capacity. I'm settling on autoscaling-pathology as the primary explanation with about 0.85 confidence.

hypotheses.subject: io-shop autoscaler / replica capacity
hypotheses.summary: Traffic to io-shop rose (request_volume climbing from ~1200/min to a plateau of 5400/min starting ~21:46) and the autoscaler kept adding and then immediately reclaiming capacity: cpu_limit_cores flaps between 3.0 and 6.0 every 1-3 minutes (3→6→3→6...) straight through the incident, even after request_volume flattens out at 5400 from 21:56 onward. Each time capacity drops back to 3 cores while cpu_used_cores is pegged at or above 3, p50/p95/p99 latency spike into the hundreds/thousands of ms (e.g. p99 3193ms at 22:04 with cpu_limit_cores=3.0), then partially recover when the limit jumps back to 6. This is the signature of a scaling controller that will not settle rather than of capacity simply being outgrown - a plateaued, sized-once capacity would hold one value, not oscillate after demand stopped climbing.

An alternative reading of the same climb: request_volume grew roughly 4.5x (1200→5400/min) in about 10 minutes, well beyond what the service's steady 3-core baseline was provisioned for, and the resulting queuing produced the latency spikes seen from 21:52 onward. This is weaker than the autoscaling explanation because cpu_limit_cores is not held at a single value throughout - it visibly toggles between 3.0 and 6.0 - which is the specific signal that points to a controller not settling rather than plain undersizing.

No deploys or config/flag changes were recorded anywhere in the two hours before or during the incident, and the rollout is fully converged on a single revision, so code, configuration, and in-flight rollout splits are all ruled out. The account-page ClientDisconnected errors in the logs are a symptom of shoppers timing out on the slow responses, not a distinct root cause; io-pricing/io-pay latency isn't implicated since nothing in the logs points at those dependencies specifically.

supporting_evidence.claim: Deployment of io-shop has converged: all 3 replicas are running the same revision.
